defaults.teacher_persona: An analyst who builds decision support for operations teams and refuses to ship a number without its definition and its uncertainty.
classmates: A business manager who wants a single number to act on
A data steward who worries about where the data came from and who cleaned it
defaults.interaction: Case-based: the teacher works one real question end to end, then the peers repeat the move on their own data question.
defaults.assessment: Each classroom ends with 3-5 checks aligned to the chapter's graded activity.

classrooms.title: From a Question to a Measurable Spec
classrooms.prompt: Start from three fuzzy business questions ('are we losing customers?', 'which shift is slowest?', 'did the training help?'). The teacher turns the first into a measurable spec: decision, population, time window, metric definition, exclusions, and what answer would change the decision. The classmates do the same for the other two, then challenge each other's definitions. Include slides on why a metric needs an owner and a definition, a roleplay where two teams report different numbers for 'churn', and a quiz on which question is answerable with the available data. Close with the spec template.
objectives: Turn a vague question into a measurable spec
Define a metric, its population, and its exclusions
Spot when a question cannot be answered with the data at hand

classrooms.title: What a Model Can and Cannot Tell You
classrooms.prompt: Use a simple, concrete case: a model that predicts which customers will leave. The teacher separates prediction from explanation and from causation, shows why a base rate matters, and demonstrates how a model can be accurate overall and useless for the small group the team cares about. The peers examine a supplied confusion matrix and decide where the model helps and where it must not be used. Include slides on correlation versus cause, a roleplay where a vendor claims the model 'proves' the training worked, and a quiz on which claim the evidence supports.
objectives: Read a confusion matrix and a base rate
Refuse a causal claim the evidence does not support

activities.title: Where may this model be used

classrooms.title: Cleaning, Describing, Charting — With Checks
classrooms.prompt: Run an assisted analysis on a supplied messy table: the teacher shows how to profile the data, list the cleaning decisions, describe the distribution, and choose a chart that answers the question. Then the AI produces a confident summary with one wrong total and one misleading chart. The peers find both, recompute the total from the table, and rewrite the caption. Include slides on checkable analysis steps, a roleplay where an AI-generated chart hides an excluded group, and a quiz on which summary sentence is supported by the data. Emphasize: recompute every number that will be quoted.
objectives: Profile a messy table before analyzing it
Record cleaning decisions so the result is reproducible
Recompute any number that will be quoted

classrooms.title: Reporting for a Decision
classrooms.prompt: Turn an analysis into a one-page decision memo. The teacher shows the structure (decision, evidence, uncertainty, options, recommendation, what would change our mind) and rewrites a rambling AI summary into it. The peers draft a memo from a supplied result set, then swap and red-team each other's uncertainty statements. Include slides on honest uncertainty and on charts that survive a screenshot, a roleplay where an executive asks for a single number and no caveats, and a short assessment on which memo is decision-ready.
objectives: Write a decision memo with evidence and uncertainty
State what would change the recommendation

activities.title: A memo that supports a decision
